messages:
emma: Customer reported that their service-account tokens stayed valid after requesting a revoke via the UI. They included a curl call and claim the UI showed success but keys still work. Escalating — sounds like a tool/function routing issue.
ryan: can you paste the payload they sent? autorouter logs first?
emma: pasted below. short version: user clicked 'revoke' in console -> backend call goes to /tools/exec -> autorouter picked `create_service_account` somehow. payload: ```{
  \"action\": \"revoke\",
  \"target\": \"service_account\",
  \"id\": \"svc-4f2a9\",
  \"reason\": \"compromised\"
}```
emma: UI shows 200 and message "Service account revoked" but customer hit tokens are still accepted.
sre-bot: autorouter executed: create_service_account(id=svc-4f2a9) - confidence=0.62 - matched signature: (name:string, id:string, meta:object?)
ryan: that confidence is dangerously low. looks like signature overlap: both create and revoke accept an `id` and `target` sometimes, and `reason` is optional string. we need repro.
maya: assigning to eng-runtime. this is P1 for customer security. Maya -> can you confirm whether our create handler returns success that the UI interprets as revoke?
jon: quick repro: ran the exact payload above against the exec endpoint in staging. got 200, body {"result":"ok","action":"create","id":"svc-4f2a9"} and a new account was created with same id (collision), old tokens still valid. logs: ```[2026-01-15T14:33:21Z] autorouter: matched create_service_account via fuzzy match (payload keys match subset).```
ryan: ok reproduction confirmed. root cause hypothesis: the function signatures for create_service_account and revoke_service_account both include `id` and optional `meta`/`reason` in our tool registry; the autorouter fuzzy matcher is preferring creation when `action` is a free-text field rather than an explicit enum.
emma: customer impact: tokens not revoked -> security exposure. they rotated keys manually as mitigation. customer wants root cause and fix ETA.
maya: short-term mitigations: 1) mark revoke_service_account as higher priority fallback in routing table for requests containing `action: revoke` 2) add a validation step that requires explicit `op` enum for destructive ops (revoke/delete) 3) apply a quick patch to UI to send `tool_hint: revoke_service_account` in payload.
ryan: for a permanent fix we should: - tighten signatures (revoke should require `force:true` boolean or `requested_by:string`) - improve autorouter to respect explicit action fields and hard block when `action` maps to known destructive verbs - add unit tests for signature collisions.
jon: logging note: will add audit hooks so any create vs revoke calls include the original payload in our trace (redacted sensitive fields) and emit a high-severity alert when a create happens immediately after a supposed revoke.
emma: I told the customer we have a mitigation and eng will follow up. they asked for repro steps and a minimal test case — included above.
maya: tagging on-call runtime: @ryan can you own the hotfix? aim for a short rollback-safe change: prefer explicit `action` match before fuzzy signature, ship to staging, run the customer repro, then prod.
ryan: will do. starting with a unit test that replicates the exact payload collision. I'll push a staged change and post the deploy bot output here.
jon: deploy-bot: staging deploy queued for runtime/autorouter at sha 7f3d2b.
ryan: good to go, will post updates. :lock:
emma: thanks all — will keep customer updated and post CC once prod patch is out.
